 Print Deepinder Goyal has announced six color options for Temple, his upcoming health wearable device Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal has shared a new update on Temple, the hardware venture he has been teasing in recent months, announcing that pre-orders for the first batch of the device will open on November 1. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), Goyal wrote, “The wait is over. Temple Batch 01 pre orders open November 1. Each @temple is hand-made to order and delivered to you within three months of your purchase." Along with announcing the pre-order date, Goyal also indicated that the company is taking a measured approach to scaling production. According to Goyal, Temple is following a "grow slow" strategy, with a focus on maintaining quality control and ensuring customers receive a strong experience. "Quality control, and also making sure we serve each customer well. Following the 'grow slow' approach with temple," Goyal said while explaining the company's approach to fulfilling orders. Hand-made units, three-month delivery timeline
 The latest update suggests that Temple's first production batch will be manufactured to order rather than mass-produced. Goyal said every unit will be hand-made, with deliveries expected within three months of purchase. The announcement gives potential buyers their first clear timeline for ordering the device, while also signalling that availability may remain limited during the initial phase as the company prioritises production quality over rapid expansion. It will come in six colours, with Real Jade, Deep Blue and Purple Funk marked as limited editions. Temple has not yet announced pricing, the number of devices in the first batch, or the exact date deliveries will begin, and said it would share more information before pre-orders open. What Temple does
 Temple is an experimental health-tech wearable developed under a private initiative backed by Goyal. It uses optical sensors to track changes in cerebral blood flow, a metric the company calls BrainFlow. The device tracks blood flow and oxygenation inside the brain. The wearable first drew attention when Goyal appeared on a podcast in early 2026 wearing a small metallic clip-like device on his head. The road to launch
 In May, Goyal announced that the first 100 devices were ready to ship to select founding users, including athletes, scientists, doctors, founders and creators. In August, he said the latest version was less than half the size of the one shown earlier, and claimed it was the smallest wearable on the market by volume and the most powerful. Independent reports noted that he gave no hardware specifications or performance data to back that claim. At that time, he said the limited launch edition would ship before the end of 2026. The new three-month delivery window suggests that orders placed from November 1 could reach customers in early 2027.
